spec_match.rationale: The spec column is derived directly from the fetched grammar none | [ [before|after] || [links|tabs] ] — including the ||-order and omission rules — and the invalid rows encode what that grammar forbids, independent of any browser.

interactive.rationale: The matrix runs 13 real declarations through CSS.supports, setProperty retention, and getComputedStyle on demand; the cascade stage rewrites a live stylesheet from two checkboxes and the carousel's marker row appears/disappears accordingly.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index card promises the matrix plus the dropped-declaration cascade behaviour; both stages deliver it.

edge_cases.rationale: This page is the edge-case angle: spec-invalid combinations, reordered keywords, an unknown keyword, disagreement highlighting between parser and spec, and the no-fallback failure mode that silently removes the marker group in pre-154 browsers.

references.rationale: Chromestatus entry, the propdef grammar section, and css-syntax-3 error handling for the dropped-declaration behaviour.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite's supports/round-trip/rejection assertions are the immutable subset of this matrix; spec-valid values this build rejects fail there honestly rather than being weakened.

runtime_evidence.rationale: CDP run on Chromium 141: matrix reported 5 of 13 accepted with 4 spec-disagreements flagged amber; cascade stage verified all four checkbox states (after tabs wins; mode-only keeps after tabs; none when empty; after links when base-only), zero console errors, desktop + 360px screenshots read.

telemetry_health.rationale: matrix-can-return-false asserts on the guaranteed-false invalid rows (the probe cannot be structurally true), and the cascade asserts cover both the group-present and no-declaration branches.

design_system.rationale: Verdict colours emerald/rose/amber only on near-white cells; the run button and checkbox rows follow the shared control styling; all colours are variables.

accessibility.rationale: The matrix is a real table with caption and scoped headers, statuses are aria-live outputs, checkboxes are native inputs inside large labelled hit areas, and the live CSS block carries an aria-label.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Matrix table scrolls inside its own container (min-width 640px), page scrollWidth stays 360 under mobile emulation, checkbox rows are 44px, and the carousel behaves identically at both widths.

guidanceConsulted.query: CSS invalid declaration fallback progressive enhancement
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Ship progressive declarations: the older-syntax declaration first, the newer one after, relying on CSS error recovery to drop only what a parser cannot read.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The cascade stage teaches exactly this pattern and the page's own carousels use it (base 'after' first, mode declaration second); the snippet block states the pre-154 consequence of omitting the base line.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive data table without horizontal overflow
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Wide tables belong in their own overflow-x auto container; the page body must never scroll horizontally.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The 5-column matrix lives in a .scroller with overflow-x auto; verified scrollWidth 360 under mobile emulation.

openQuestions.title: Re-run the matrix on Chrome 154 and update the disagreement copy if it hits zero
openQuestions.detail: On the build browser 4 spec-valid rows (links, tabs, tabs after, links before) read false. On a real Chrome 154 the matrix should agree on all 13 rows; confirm that and capture the screenshot so the amber-disagreement path has a recorded zero-state too.

summary: Edge-case angle: a 13-value grammar matrix with three independent oracles and spec-vs-browser disagreement highlighting, plus a live cascade demo proving the dropped-declaration fallback pattern that makes the mode keywords safe to ship today.
